```plato
//==
// # Splines
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Evaluating the Bezier splines
//  - Knot vectors and B-spline / NURBS domains
//  - Piecewise indexing and Hermite evaluation
//  - Evaluating the interpolating splines
//  - Deformation bodies for the control-point curves

library Splines
{
    //==
    // # Evaluating the Bezier splines
    //
    // Evaluation of the control-point curves declared in `splines.types.plato`.
    // De Casteljau's algorithm is the whole story: it is generic in `$T`, using it
    // only through Lerp, so one reduction serves points, vectors, and weights, and
    // the rational form is that same reduction run twice. Nothing from
    // `library Polynomials` is reimplemented here.

    //==
    // # Bezier curves of arbitrary degree
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Casteljau%27s_algorithm
    // De Casteljau's algorithm is the one Bezier evaluator that does not need a
    // closed form per degree: repeatedly replace the control values by the
    // lerps of adjacent pairs until one remains. It only needs Lerp, so it is
    // generic in the type variable `$T` and serves points, vectors, and
    // weights — and that genericity is now SPELLED, by the function's own
    // `where` clause (plato-393).

    // The de Casteljau reduction of a control polygon at t.
    // Precondition: xs is non-empty.
    //
    // Written ONCE, over `$T`. The body needs Lerp on a bare element, and the `where` clause is
    // what promises it: the element type of the array must be IInterpolatable, so the call is
    // licensed at the declaration, every call site is checked against the bound (an
    // `Array<String>` is rejected), and the emitted C# carries the matching constraint instead of
    // a throwing stub. Before plato-393 this was five hand-copied bodies — Point2D, Point3D,
    // Vector2D, Vector3D, Number — because a bound could only be inherited from a constructed type
    // in the signature, and the only one here is `Array<T>`, which is unbounded and must stay so.
    DeCasteljau(xs: Array<$T>, t: Number): $T where $T: IInterpolatable
        => xs.Count <= 1
           ? xs[0]
           : (xs.Count - 1).MapRange(i => xs[i].Lerp(xs[i + 1], t)).DeCasteljau(t);
```
